components.cost_effect: The dual solve and A/A* applications are separately charged.
components.goal: Obtain a smooth gradient interface for the explicit max term.
components.name: Regularized dual maximizer and adjoint gradient
components.operation: Solve the regularized dual maximum and apply A* to its optimizer.
components.requires: Exact structured inner solve and the mathematical assumptions in the selected variant.
transfer_checks: Approximate inner solves require a new gradient-error analysis.
Changing the dual representation changes operator norms, prox diameter and evaluation cost.
Any added f_hat needs separate regularity and cost accounting.

content.family: dual regularization of an explicit max representation

limitations.statement: The component requires the explicit representation and exact regularized dual solving capability. It is not a generic simulation from a black-box subgradient oracle.
No generic inner-solver implementation, complexity or approximate-solve tolerance is supplied by the selected source anchors.

performance_links.scope_note: Only smoothness and uniform bias of the exact max-term evaluator; no outer iteration or unrestricted Oracle Complexity guarantee.

variants.cost: Per evaluation charge one application of A to x, one exact regularized dual solve, one application of A* for the gradient, and value/pairing evaluations needed to return f_mu. Internal evaluations, arithmetic and memory of the dual solve are additional and representation-dependent; they are not one free subgradient call. Norm/prox normalization and computation of D2, if needed, are preprocessing resources. No uniform running-time or Oracle Complexity bound is supplied here.
variants.implementation_details_ref: §2 PDF/printed p6 (2.4)–(2.6); p7 (2.7); structured-access discussion p5
variants.name: Exact regularized-max evaluation
variants.output: For each query x: u_mu(x)∈Q2, scalar f_mu(x), and g_mu(x)∈E1*. No primal minimizer or optimization accuracy certificate is produced.
public_inputs: Finite-dimensional real normed spaces E1,E2; A:E1→E2* and its adjoint.
Nonempty compact convex Q2, continuous convex phi_hat, continuous sigma2-strongly convex d2 on Q2, sigma2>0 and min_Q2 d2=0.
mu>0 and query point x∈E1; D2=max_Q2 d2 if a numerical bias certificate is wanted.
variants.query_and_update: Given x, compute b=Ax. Obtain the unique u_mu(x)=argmax_{u∈Q2}{<b,u>2-phi_hat(u)-mu d2(u)}. Return u_mu(x), f_mu(x)=<b,u_mu(x)>2-phi_hat(u_mu(x))-mu d2(u_mu(x)), and g_mu(x)=A*u_mu(x). There is no further update.
variants.requirements: The mathematical conditions are those of thm.P006.smooth_lemma. Computational use additionally requires evaluating Ax, phi_hat and d2, solving max_{u∈Q2}(<Ax,u>2-phi_hat(u)-mu d2(u)) exactly, and applying A*. A closed form for the unregularized maximum alone does not establish access to the regularized maximum.
variants.state_and_initialization: Stateless evaluator. Fix the supplied representation, norms and mu. Normalize the supplied prox function by subtracting its minimum; the prox center u0 minimizes d2. No outer iterate sequence or starting x is specified by this component.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: mu is a fixed positive public input. Evaluation ends when the exact inner maximizer and requested value/gradient are obtained; no generic inner stopping rule is supplied by (2.5). Equation (2.7) certifies bias at most mu D2. As a local algebraic consequence, for a desired bias delta>0 and known D2>0, any 0<mu≤delta/D2 suffices; if D2=0 the bias is zero for every mu>0. This is not an outer optimization stopping rule.

summary: A stateless structured evaluator: solve the strongly regularized dual maximum exactly and apply A* to return the smoothed gradient. Inner optimization is a separately charged capability.
title: Explicit max smoothing evaluator
use_when: The explicit max representation and an exact regularized inner solver are available. A generic subgradient oracle alone does not provide this interface.
